payload.feature:
Close issue #231: a promoted capability spec does not name the change that wrote it, so the trail runs one way. The operator ruled this on 2026-09-06 and it is recorded as an addendum to decision 0042 (PR #232); this run is the enactment.

Read the issue, decision 0042 with its addendum, and the first change to complete the machine, `2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i`, which promoted eight capabilities and names itself in none of them.

**The ruling, already accepted, in the operator's words:** the archive step appends one `## Provenance` line per capability it touched, appended and never rewritten, and pre-ruling archives are backfilled once by the enacting slice.

**Build it so:**

1. **The dialect's `archive` instruction does the appending.** It is the step that folds a change into standing truth, so it is the step that records which change wrote which capability. One line per capability the change touched, appended to that capability's spec; existing provenance lines are never rewritten or reordered, because standing truth accumulates and does not get edited into a different meaning.
2. **The backfill happens once, in this slice**, over the archives that predate the ruling — `2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i` and any other archived change — so every promoted capability names at least one change from the day this lands.
3. **A test that every capability's provenance list is non-empty and resolves**: each named change exists under the archive, and no capability is left without one. That test is what keeps the trail two-way after this slice.
4. **Rationale is not duplicated into standing truth.** A provenance line is a pointer, not a summary: it names the change and nothing else. The whole point of decision 0042's two-directory model is that the why lives in the change and the truth lives in the spec.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. Do not push and do not open a pull request; the operator lands it. Say what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

Reviewed 0513205 (the run's only commit) against decision 0042's addendum of 2026-09-06, which I read in full. The enactment matches the ruling point for point: dialect.v3 lands beside v1/v2 with v2's bytes untouched (frozen_contracts pins both); the archive operation gains a required `instructions` path; the OpenSpec dialect names openspec/archive.md and spec-kit keeps its archive unsupported; the implement prompt renders the instruction; the eight capabilities promoted by 2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i are backfilled with one appended line each; and crates/brokkr-cli/tests/provenance.rs asserts a non-empty, resolving, end-held `## Provenance` section per capability. Constraint compliance: no frozen contract, policy table, reference or corpus byte moves; the two dialect trees stay byte-identical (packaging.rs walks both); no literal digest is pinned anywhere in the repo, so nothing needed re-pinning; no new test drives a boxed step. Rationale is not duplicated into the specs -- each backfilled line is a pointer only.

Evidence I ran on the host: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` all green, 65 binaries, 0 failures, provenance.rs passing; `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify` both succeed.

Three findings remain, none security. I fixed none of them; I am read-only.

1. MEDIUM (correctness/compatibility) crates/brokkr-runtime/src/dialect.rs:250-259 and contracts/README.md:120-122. The comment justifying the v3-only read says v2 landed "before a journal pinned a dialect for a resume to reload"; that is not true here. realms.json has declared `"dialect": "openspec"` since 0fbfb0b (2026-09-04), engine.rs:348 pins the resolved dialect content into every run manifest, and engine.rs:455 rehydrates that world on resume through realms.rs:488 `Dialect::parse`. The openspec dialect has been `brokkr.dialect/v2` on main since 7e129da (2026-09-05, so the comment's "2026-09-04" is also off by a day). Once this build ships, resuming any run whose manifest pins the v2 dialect is refused. Worse, the refusal does not name the version: typed deserialization runs before `check()`, and a v2-shaped `archive` (`{"argv": [...]}`, no `instructions`) matches neither arm of the untagged `ArchiveOrUnsupported`, so the operator gets `WorldError::Unpinned("... data did not match any variant of untagged enum ArchiveOrUnsupported")` instead of "it calls itself 'brokkr.dialect/v2'; this build reads brokkr.dialect/v3". The new test at dialect/tests.rs asserts exactly that serde string, so this is confirmed by the change's own test; the version-boundary test `every_checked_dialect_boundary_is_named` only mutates the `schema` string on an otherwise-v3 body, so it never exercises a real v2 file. Confirmed by code path; I could not open a journal from this worktree (.forge/forge.db is per-checkout and absent here) to point at a stored v2 pin, so the existence of affected journals is inferred from the history above rather than observed. This is fail-closed, hence no security dimension, but it strands resumes and records a justification that does not hold -- the operator should either accept a v2-pinned run becoming unresumable and say so plainly, or keep a compatibility read.

2. LOW (test-coverage) crates/brokkr-cli/tests/provenance.rs. The trail is walked one way only: specs -> archive. A capability that already exists and is touched by a later fold that forgets to append a line still passes, because its list is non-empty from an earlier change. The converse walk -- for each directory under openspec/changes/archive/, every capability in its `specs/` deltas that still lives under openspec/specs/ names it -- is the assertion that would actually catch the archive step skipping the append, which is the failure this slice exists to prevent. Only a brand-new capability is caught today. The ruling's enforcement binding is worded exactly as implemented, so this is a gap in reach, not a deviation.

3. LOW (test-coverage) crates/brokkr-cli/tests/provenance.rs. Nothing asserts the shape of a provenance line beyond "list item with a backticked token that resolves". `- `x` -- folded 2026-09-06, and here is why it was done` passes. Ruling 1's "the change's archived directory name and the date it was folded", and the framing's constraint that a line is a pointer and not a summary, are enforced only by prompt prose to the smith; a date-form and trailing-content assertion would bind them.

Could not verify: the exact-coverage gate. `bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh` was refused by the sandbox, so I have no measured coverage number for the new lines in dialect.rs. By inspection every new branch has a caller -- the `ArchiveOrUnsupported::Unsupported` arms in `instruction_paths` and in `prompt_for("implement")` are reached by speckit, which both shipped-dialect tests load and render; the `UnreadableInstruction` arm for the archive path has its own new assertion; the `check_command_tokens` archive arm is reached by openspec -- but that is reasoning, not a measurement, and CI must supply it. I also could not read issue #231 itself (no GitHub access granted this session); I reviewed against decision 0042's addendum and the task framing, which restate the ruling.

One disclosed out-of-scope edit: landing_shape.rs now passes `-c commit.gpgsign=false` to its scratch repo. It is unrelated to provenance, but it is named in the commit message, mirrors delivered_by_brokkr.rs, and only stops a test inheriting the host's signing config. Not a finding.

Returned implement: answered the three residual findings the review left on 0513205 (the provenance enactment), in one commit 478d9a6 on fire/231-provenance. (1) MEDIUM, confirmed: realms.json has declared "dialect": "openspec" since 544f1d8 (2026-09-04) and engine.rs pins the resolved dialect into every run manifest, so runs pinned brokkr.dialect/v1 and v2 bodies; the v3-only read stranded their resumes, and refused with an untagged serde variant mismatch rather than by version. A dialect FILE is now read at v3 and only v3 (Dialect::parse), so the addendum's archive instruction cannot be escaped by writing an older label; a dialect PIN is read at v1, v2 or v3 (Dialect::parse_pinned), which realms.rs rehydrates with. Both read the version from the bytes before they are given a shape, so an unread version is refused BY ITS VERSION. Each version is held to its own shape: tool.install absent at v1 and required from v2; archive instructions absent below v3 and required at v3 — so an older dialect folds exactly as it did when pinned. New tests: the_older_dialect_versions_a_run_may_have_pinned_still_read (dialect) and a_run_that_pinned_an_older_dialect_still_rehydrates_its_world (realms, via World::from_manifest, the actual resume path). (2) LOW: provenance.rs now walks archive-to-specs as well as specs-to-archive, which is the direction that catches a fold that promoted a delta and forgot the append. (3) LOW: the line's shape is now asserted literally — one backticked change name, ' — folded ', a bare YYYY-MM-DD, nothing after — so 'a pointer, not a summary' is no longer prose-only. Prose corrected where it was false: the dialect.rs justification comment and the contracts/README.md paragraph both claimed no journal pins a dialect for a resume; docs/guides/versioning.md gains a dialect row naming the two surfaces.

Evidence run on the host, all after the final edit: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast exit 0, 65 suite summaries, none with a nonzero failure count; brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self and --bundle bundles/verify both exit 0 with empty stderr. Exact coverage MEASURED this time, not reasoned: scripts/coverage-exact.sh itself is refused by the seat sandbox, so I ran its steps by hand on the pinned nightly-2026-09-05 (cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --locked --branch, then the report to LCOV) and reimplemented its awk arithmetic in python: lines 21399/21399, branches 3350/3350, functions 2028/2028 — literal integer equality — and the harness-leak jq check returns true. No frozen contract, policy table, reference or corpus byte moved; no witness or compose digest moved (the change is Rust source and prose only, and witness_digests.rs passes untouched); no new test drives a boxed step.

One thing the operator should rule on, which I did not do myself: decision 0042's addendum of 2026-09-04 records inside its enforcement binding that "this build reads brokkr.dialect/v2 only, which costs nothing today ... no journal pins a v1 dialect for a resume to reload". That was untrue within a day of being written (544f1d8 declared the dialect on 2026-09-04, 7e129da raised it to v2 on 2026-09-05). I did not edit an accepted decision; I changed the reader so the claim's intent — that a version bump costs nothing — now holds. If the operator would rather the binding be amended to say files are v3 and pins are version-tolerant, that is an addendum, not this commit.

Not verified: remote CI on this head, and anything requiring GitHub (I could not read issue #231 itself; I worked from decision 0042 with its addendum, which restates the ruling, and from the task framing).

Reviewed 0513205..478d9a6 (27 files) against the framing and decision 0042's addendum of 2026-09-06. The ruling is enacted where it belongs: the dialect's archive command carries `instructions`, the instruction is dialect data (`openspec/archive.md`), it is pinned by `Dialect::load`/`render` and rendered into the smith's implement prompt, and the resume path takes `rendered` from the pin so no prompt is recovered from a mutable file. Backfill is complete and exact -- 8 archived deltas, 8 living capabilities, one line each. The two-way test is stronger than the binding asked for: the archive-to-specs walk catches the fold that promotes a delta and forgets the append, which the specs-to-archive walk alone would pass, and `named_change` holds the line to a pointer (one backticked name, ` -- folded `, a bare YYYY-MM-DD, nothing after), so 'rationale is not duplicated into standing truth' is tested rather than asserted. The v1/v2 pin-reading widening in 478d9a6 is justified and I confirmed it: realms.json first declared `"dialect": "openspec"` at 544f1d8 while `dialects/openspec.json` still said v1 (v2 landed later at 7e129da), so v1 and v2 bodies really were pinned, and the v1 file shape differs from v2 only by `tool.install`, so today's struct reads it. Reading the version from the raw bytes before deserialization is the right call -- an untagged archive enum would otherwise have refused a v2 pin as a serde variant mismatch. `tool.install` becoming Option is safe: it has no production consumer outside dialect.rs, and the version gate re-requires it from v2 on.

SECURITY: none. No new injection surface -- the archive instruction path goes through the same spelling-only relative-path gate as every other instruction (it is included in `instruction_paths`, which I checked), it is read once at pin time and never re-read on resume, and its content is covered by `instructions_sha256`. The pin reader is widened, but a manifest tamperer already controls the pinned `rendered` map wholesale, so accepting an older `schema` label grants no new power; the FILE surface stays fail-closed at v3, so a v2 label cannot be written today to escape the instruction requirement. Frozen bytes untouched: contracts v1/v2, realms, seat-record, policy/phase-machine.json, reference/ and fixtures/ are unchanged; dialect.v3 lands as a new file beside them and is pinned by frozen_contracts.rs.

TWO LOW RESIDUALS, neither returned:

1. low, correctness/instruction-fidelity -- `dialects/openspec/archive.md:14` (and its byte-identical copy `crates/brokkr-cli/dialects/openspec/archive.md:14`) states the provenance template as a single-backtick code span containing backslash-escaped backticks: `- \`<archived-directory-name>\` -- folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Backslash escapes are inert inside a CommonMark code span, and the prompt delivers this as raw text, so the one artifact whose job is to state the format tells the smith to write literal backslashes. A smith copying it faithfully produces a line `named_change` (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/provenance.rs:36) rejects on `strip_prefix("- `")`, so the fold's own instruction can generate the shape the gate refuses. Fails loudly here, but for any other realm adopting this dialect the rule is prose-only and there is no gate. The other two statements of the format are correct -- the ```text fence in provenance.rs and the eight backfilled lines -- so the fix is to use the same fenced block.

2. low, documentation/governance -- decision 0042's addendum of 2026-09-04 still ends its enforcement binding with 'This build reads `brokkr.dialect/v2` only, which costs nothing today: the dialect landed the same day with no realm declaring one, so no journal pins a v1 dialect for a resume to reload' (docs/decisions/0042...md:573-575). After this slice the build reads v3 from a file and v1/v2/v3 from a pin, and 478d9a6's own commit message records that the stated reason 'was never true'. The accepted decision now contradicts the code with no marker, in a realm whose premise is that decisions are authoritative; the repo already has the mechanism for exactly this (the `## Erratum` heading on decision 0043, pinned by openspec/specs/boundary-guides/spec.md). The implementer correctly declined to edit an accepted decision, so this is left for the operator's ruling rather than returned. Prose elsewhere is consistent -- contracts/README.md and docs/guides/versioning.md both record the file-versus-pin split.

Info, not a finding: 478d9a6 also bundles an unrelated test-hygiene fix, `crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/landing_shape.rs` forcing `commit.gpgsign=false` on its temp repository. Legitimate and consistent with delivered_by_brokkr.rs, but outside the ruling's scope.

EVIDENCE I RAN on the committed tree: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test provenance` 2/2 ok; `cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib dialect::` 11/11 ok; `--test sdd_shape --test frozen_contracts --test witness_digests` all ok (witness digests unmoved, so nothing needed re-pinning); `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify` both exit 0. Full-suite evidence relied on the implement seat's .forge/test-full-final.log (65 'test result: ok', no FAILED), recorded after the last source edit.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY: (a) the exact-coverage gate -- I did not re-run the instrumented build. The recorded report (.forge/cov, exact.py over target/coverage/lcov.info) reads 21399/21399 lines, 3350/3350 branches, 2028/2028 functions, and its instrumented extent for dialect.rs ends at line 637, which is the closing brace of `library_path` in the committed file, so the report is line-aligned with what was committed; but the report was produced at 01:32:39 and dialect.rs was last touched at 01:33:49, so the alignment is strong evidence, not proof. (b) `openspec validate --archived --strict --no-interactive`, the dialect's own verify command, over the specs now carrying a `## Provenance` section -- the sandbox refused to run the binary and refused to read the installed package, so whether OpenSpec's strict spec parser tolerates an unrecognised `## Provenance` section at the end of a living spec.md is untested here. It would surface on the next SDD run's verify step, not in cargo test. Worth the operator or CI running once before this lands.
